About Shasun

Home

About

About Shasun

Premier Institution of Higher Learning for Women

Shri Shankarlal Sundarbai Shasun Jain College for Women has been recognized as premier institution of higher learning for women. A centre for academic excellence and achievement, it is today one of the finest institutions for Sciences, Humanities and commerce affiliated to the University of Madras.

The College has a rich legacy. Established in 2005, with a generous contribution made by Smt.Sundarbai Shankarlal Charitable Trust, T. Nagar, Chennai of the SHASUN Family and Group, the institution provides a unique opportunity to young women for quality higher education. In this, they were abetted by the founders, who were independent minded with a deep concern for quality of education they wished to impart. These attributes of total dedication have contributed in a large measure to the position of distinction occupied by the college. The College management is committed to creating an atmosphere in which the zest for learning thrives and students are trained not only academically but also to be women of convictions and values. All programmes are student-centred, providing ample opportunity for the development of leadership and self-assurance.

College History

Sri Swetambar Stanakwasi Jain Educational Society (Regd.) was founded in the year 1937. The society has been rendering yeomen service to the community by nurturing learning experience and enabling students to realize their inherent potential and to mould them into competent, self-reliant and socially responsible citizens.

In the seven decades of its presence, the Society has been responsible for successfully establishing several educational institutions like:

Mohan mull Chordia Jain Industrial Training Centre.

Sri AgurchandManmull Jain College.

Sri Tarachand Galada Jain Vidyalaya.

Sri Mangichand Bhandari Jain Higher Secondary School.

Sri AmoluckChand Galada Jain Higher Secondary School.

Sri Badalchand Sayarchand Chordia Jain Vidyalaya.

A. M Jain School.

The Management Committee of the College consists of eminent industrialists, philanthropists, academicians and administrators of repute. With their constant guidance and encouragement, the College is confident of converting itself into an institution of excellence.

The college was granted permission by the Govt. of Tamilnadu by its G.O on 16th September, 2004 and affiliation by the University of Madras on 18th May 2005.

title: Academic Overview
text:
Academic Overview

Home

Academics

Academic overview

Shri Shankarlal Sundarbai Shasun Jain College for Women is an Arts and Science college located in Chennai, Tamil Nadu. It is affiliated with the University of Madras.

Located at the cutting edge of knowledge, Shri Shankarlal Sundarbai Shasun Jain College for Women has not just kept pace with the changing world, but has been the pioneering spirit behind many innovations in the field of education. The striving is to imbue the teaching / learning process with a unique blend of intellectual rigour and aesthetic and ethical engagement, The Shasun Campus has excellent infrastructural facilities and is always alive with activity – academic, co-curricular, extra-curricular and sports. Our students are expected to participate actively and to take advantage of the many opportunities offered, so that they can develop into self-confident, responsible, ethical and compassionate human beings.

It welcomes interaction with other colleges and educational organizations, actively engaging the women in all its extramural activities, competing with the best on equal terms. The extremely distinguished list of alumnae imparts a sense of confidence and immense pride in students. They view themselves as torchbearers of great traditions. All this propels them to often explore uncharted territory and think unfettered to create a better world, especially for women. Welcome to Shasun!

CBCS SYSTEM

Our college follows the Choice-Based Credit System, which is a flexible system of learning. The distinguishing features of CBCS are the following:

It permits students to learn at their own pace

Choose electives from a wide range of elective courses offered by the University .

Undergo additional courses and acquire more than the required number of credits .

Adopt an inter-disciplinary and intra-disciplinary approach in learning.

Make best use of the expertise of available faculty.

Value added courses

Shasun has almost 5 value added courses namely Certified Industrial accountant, Step program, Advanced Excel, E- filing and like Skills from Aparajitha foundations. When Shasuneoens live life in alignment with a purpose that is centred on selflessly adding values for others, opportunities become abundant and life becomes fulfilled.

Collaborations

The College has signed MoU’s and is actively engaged with various professional bodies like, Hindustan Chamber of Commerce , Andhra Chamber of Commerce – Madras Chamber of Commerce – Kancheepuram Nippon Chamber of Commerce -,NDL – National Digital Library – PROQUEST – N-LIST ,Our institution in total has facilitated 33 MoU’s and 8 new have been initiated with industries and institutions in this year, which includes The Hindu Group-STEP , MESC |,Global Theoretical Research , Tamil Nadu Teachers education University | Pantech-e-learning | Aparjitha | M/S ICA EDU Skills Pvt. Ltd | Institute of Cost Accountant of India | Madras Management Association.

OBE at Shasun College

Change is the only constant today, and with it, comes the need for education systems to update and adapt their approach or risk becoming obsolete altogether. Outcome-Based Education (OBE) is a pedagogical model that entails the restructuring of curriculum, pedagogy, and assessment practices to reflect the achievement of high-order learning with a student-centric approach.

Out Come Based Education is a learning paradigm that focuses on the outcomes or goals instead of results. Having realized the importance of OBE and its implementation, the institution, ventured into OBE concepts in the academic year 2018-19.

The faculty sets a certain number of necessary skills and knowledge that the learner should possess at the end of education and they are identified as the outcomes. The assessments like exams, assignments, and projects are then defined to measure the achievement of these outcomes, and their results indicate whether the students have achieved them or not by the end of their study/learning.

Our faculty guides and help the students master the material using many student-centric approaches. At an individual level, the achievement of students is used to decide what outcome they have reached. The students will also be given credits according to their performance.

Student involvement in the classroom is a key part of OBE. Students are expected to do self-learning so that they attain a full understanding of the material. Increased student involvement allows students to feel responsible for their learning. Outcome-Based Education is a necessity of the hour and it is implemented in our institution with great care to bring about a harmonious growth of the physical, emotional, social, intellectual, and spiritual qualities inherent in our students and make them into responsible future global citizens.

Economics is offered as allied subjects in major Departments (M.Com A&F, B.Com Honours, B.Com General, B.Com A& F B.Com CS B.Com BM & BBA). Economics will enable the students to understand Consumer behaviour, Business, Market, and Government. The subject helps the students to face competitive exams. Economics, at its core, is the study to evaluate alternative courses of action and how to make better choices. It develops critical thinking and problem-solving skills to make decisions. Additionally, activities like analysis of the union budget, group discussion on GDP, and other economic-related aspects will enable students to understand the real state of our economy and help the students to become strong Financial Analysts. text:
English - (Shift I)
Home
Academics
Department
Allied
Overview
Department Newsletter
Faculty
The English Department commenced in the year 2005. English language fluency is important both in studies and career. The department aims to produce competent and knowledgeable graduates who have acquired relevant language and literary skills and knowledge of English that would enable them to meet and adapt effectively to the demands of a changing global society, especially in the fields of language, literature, and education. Since its inception, the Department has acted as a beacon of hope for the students. It not only imparts soft skills; it focuses on Communicative English skills to help students improve their command of the language. The new syllabus focuses more on listening, speaking, reading, and writing. This year, a mandatory course called Professional English for Commerce and Management, Life Sciences, Physical sciences, Arts, and Sciences has also started to familiarise students with the vocabulary of their subjects.
The main aim of teaching English is to empower future graduates to function effectively in their future globalised workplace environments. The students are evaluated through a range of assessment strategies such as student presentations, mid-term tests, quizzes, course assignments, project work, and written final examination. Online lectures, Film screenings, workshops, seminars, competitions (inter and intra). Literary club activities etc. make up our calendar.

text:
Tamil - (Shift I)
Home
Academics
Department
Allied
Overview
Department Newsletter
Faculty
The Department of Tamil commenced in the year 2005 with strength of 100 students. The Department offers Tamil as Part I subject for the streams such as Commerce, Basic Sciences, and Management. The current strength of Part I Tamil students is 1413. The Department is committed to the growth of the students into holistic individuals. Through this course, one can learn about Tamil Literature, its history, and other aspects. Also, a teacher of a Tamil language is responsible for educating the students and giving them a proper knowledge of Tamil literature. Nowadays, the opportunities in Tamil are increasing at a rapid rate in various sectors. Especially, the study of Tamil prepares students to understand in a creative manner. Also, the scope of learning Tamil Literature is quite good, where one can earn respect & money both under this professional career.
The Department of Tamil has produced exemplary results and so far the pass percentage has always been 95% and above. With an objective to provide an undisturbed learning experience, Shasun has introduced a Learning Management System. Powered with collaborative workspaces, assessment features, communication channels, and e-content provisions, LMS is an advanced interactivity building tool for our institution.

title: Outcome Based Education
text:
Outcome Based Education

Home

Academics

Outcome Based Education

Graduate Attributes

The following are the graduate attributes defined for our institution.

Knowledge and understanding of the content and techniques of the selected discipline at advanced levels.

Proficiency in the appropriate use of contemporary technologies of their respective disciplines.

The ability to locate, analyse, evaluate and synthesize information from a good source in a planned and timely manner.

The ability to identify and use effective, creative and innovative solutions, both independently and cooperatively in current and future problems.

Skills of a high order in interpersonal understanding, teamwork, and communication.

An awareness of ethical, social and cultural issues in a worldwide context and their importance in the exercise of professional skills and responsibilities.

The ability to take initiatives and exhibit leadership skills.

Commitment to continuous learning and the capacity to maintain intellectual curiosity throughout life.

The ability to meet environmental and societal needs and comply with them.

Program Educational Objectives

The following are the educational objectives set by our institution.

To impart quality education for the holistic development of the undergraduate students by imparting life skills and value education.

To establish expertise in the discipline and enable them to articulate their expertise in solving problems.

To make them socially responsible and competent enough to face the challenges of life.

To engage the students for extended learning throughout their life and enable them to resolve contemporary issues evolved in ever-changing areas of arts and science.

To facilitate them to render service to the community as responsible citizens.

Programme Outcomes

PO1

Critical Thinking
: Take informed actions after identifying the assumptions that frame our thinking and actions, checking out the degree to which these assumptions are accurate and valid, and looking at our ideas and decisions (intellectual, organizational, and personal) from different perspectives.

PO2

Problem Solving
: Understand and solve problems of relevance to society to meet the specified needs using the knowledge, skills and attitudes acquired from humanities / sciences/mathematics/social sciences.

PO3

Effective Communication
: Speak, read , write and listen clearly in person and through electronic media in English and in one Indian language, and make meaning of the world by connecting people, ideas, books, media and technology.

PO4

Social Interaction
: Elicit views of others, mediate disagreements and help reach conclusions in group settings.

PO5

Effective Citizenship
: Demonstrate empathetic social concern and equity centered national development, and the ability to act with an informed awareness of issues and participate in civic life through volunteering.

PO6

Ethics
: Recognize different value systems including your own, understand the moral dimensions of your decisions, and accept responsibility for them.

PO7

Environment & Sustainability
: Understand the issues of environmental contexts and sustainable development.

PO8

Self-directed & Life-long learning
: Acquire the ability to engage in independent and life-long learning in the broadest context of socio-technological changes.

The Department of Psychology for postgraduate level (M.Sc. Applied Psychology (Specialization in counselling) was established in the year 2020-21 with a batch of 25 students. The duration of the course is two academic years. The PG program offered by the Department is affiliated with the University of Madras.
The Department periodically provides practical exposure to its students through internships, field visits, valued-added courses, seminars, workshops, and research paper presentations.
The Postgraduate course is structured specifically to train the students in various fields of Psychology through a strong theoretical foundation combined with a completely applied and practical orientation. The course will provide training in Principal domains of the discipline such as Counselling; Psychotherapy; Contemporary therapies; Social psychology; Cognitive Psychology, Neuroscience; Psychopathology, Research; Training and Development; Organisational and Workplace Counselling. The thrust is to ensure the students master the theoretical know-how, imbibe assessment and intervention skills required for the various fields of interest.
The Department also extends its service through the College Counselling Cell (Sukhada), which offers counselling and therapeutic support to all staff and students within the campus through regular one-on-one sessions, group training programs and psychological workshops.
The vision of the Department is to spread the vitality of mental health professions and create minds equipped to handle a society with varying mental health needs. The Department functions on providing a conducive environment to all its members by encouraging autonomy, inclusivity and ethical thinking. As a core approach, we are mindfully value based on our every choice and deed, believing the best way to teach is to be it yourself!
Our Vision
To create skilled and professional psychologists through comprehensive quality teaching, training and research.
Our Mission
To provide diagnosis and assessment, apply appropriate counselling techniques and develop training and intervention modules for psychosocial modifications

Shri Shankarlal Sundarbai Shasun Jain College for Women was established in the year 2005. The School of Commerce offers the Bachelor’s Programme in Commerce – B.Com Honours, General, Accounting & Finance, Corporate Secretaryship and post graduate program in M.Com (AF). School of Commerce embodies and strives to deliver world-class education in various branches of Commerce.
The School of Commerce has the state-of-the-art learning facilities for the students to impart the holistic education with a WIFI enabled campus. The college also possesses high tech labs and digital accessed e-library facilities. The school provides ample scope for creative thinking and participative learning through following an innovative pedagogy in teaching learning process through flipped classroom methodology, ERP facility, LMS and ICT enabled teaching student centric methodology. Outcome Based Education (OBE) is adopted with Program Outcome and Course Outcome for the benefit of the students.
The school has also nurtured its students to meet the expectations of the competitive corporate world and has been home for many budding entrepreneurs. The school pioneers in motivating and encouraging the students to showcase their potential and innumerable talents in various curricular & co-curricular activities & competitions. The combination of core skills and specialized knowledge provided in each programme enables students to enrich their professional and managerial skills.
Campus connects through interactive guest lectures, workshops, internships, student projects brings knowledge, skills and ability to analyze and synthesize the contemporary application oriented perspective through classroom learning. The School of Commerce has collaborated with Professional Bodies like Madras Management Association, Institute of Cost Accountants of India, Hindustan Chamber of Commerce, Andhra Chamber of Commerce, etc.
The departments provide various Add-on Courses and Certificate Courses to the students to enhance their skills on aptitude, personality and social growth of students. The courses serve the need of academics as well and prepares students for diversified fields such as business, entrepreneurship, research, teaching, human resource, finance & economic planning, etc. All programmes are a blend of theoretical thoughts, practical activities and internship training.

School of Religious Studies
Overview
Department
Faculty
Religious education reinforces the need for emphasizing respect for other living beings, regardless of their beliefs, race, social status or stage of evolution. It helps one create an atmosphere of love and acceptance. The future generations are exposed to a life embedded with values and goodness by a deeper understanding of the knowledge laid in the Holy Scriptures by our renowned saints. It nurtures deep respect for the spiritual aspect of religion and sets one up on a path of spiritual awakening. The hallmark of religious studies is a holistic development of the student and creates a balance in their life. Reduction of stress and other lifestyle related diseases is an auxiliary benefit. Religious studies teach the importance of self-introspection and how to overcome delusion and passions. It creates an optimistic attitude in students to face the challenges of life in a responsible and detached way.
Apart from pursuing careers of their choice it also helps the students
To inculcate qualities like equanimity, self-control, discipline in their daily living.
To enable them practice compassion in thoughts, words and action by simultaneously helping them to eliminate prejudice, intolerance and hate. Practice of values is encouraged.
To maintain focus on the bigger picture of life and its purpose.
To strive for success and at the same time not to get attached to the fruits of action.
To develop positive mental conditioning.
To become independent thinkers who seek to understand and improve themselves and the world around them.
To help them know their own inner self and this understanding contributes to a more just and cohesive society.
Apart from religious and spiritual upliftment, it promotes self-awareness, respect for self & others, open-mindedness, devotion, dedication, appreciation and communication; the qualities which are essential in today’s pluralistic society. Religion unifies everyone and is the center of human life. By religious studies, one can study what is essential about them in the world. Psychology is the scientific study of the mind and behaviour. Psychologists are actively involved in studying and understanding mental processes, brain functions, and behaviour. It is an academic discipline of immense scope and is one of the fastest growing profession.
With advanced training in psychology, one can choose to work in scientific research, neuroscience, clinical practice, or as a consultant in large corporations, hospitals or government agencies.
It’s difficult, if not impossible, to think of a facet of life where psychology is not involved. Psychologists employ the scientific method – stating the question, offering a theory and then constructing rigorous laboratory or field experiments to test the hypothesis. Psychologists apply the understanding gleaned through research to create evidence-based strategies that solve problems and improve lives.
The result is that psychological science unveils new and better ways for people to exist and thrive in a complex world.

The Department periodically provides practical exposure to its students through internships, field visits, value-added courses, seminars, workshops, and research paper presentations. A few regular courses offered by the Department for UG are Expressive Art therapy; Counselling Skills & techniques and Transactional Analysis based programs.
The Department also extends its service through the College Counselling Cell (Sukhada), which offers counselling and therapeutic support to all staff and students within the campus through regular one-on-one sessions, group training programs, and psychological workshops.
The vision of the Department is to spread the vitality of mental health professions and create minds equipped to handle a society with varying mental health needs. The Department functions on providing a conducive environment to all its members by encouraging autonomy, inclusivity, and ethical thinking. As a core approach, we are mindfully value based on our every choice and deed, believing the best way to teach is to be it yourself!

The Department of Visual Communication (Shift II) at Shri Shankarlal Sundarbai Shasun Jain College for Women, Chennai was started in June 2023. This new extension aims to cater to the growing demand for our highly valued BSc Visual Communication program, originally established in 2005. The Department is committed to sculpting the next generation of media professionals, creators and communicators, equipped with both theoretical knowledge and practical skills.
The department takes pride in having state-of-the-art infrastructure designed to provide students with hands-on experience and industry-relevant skills. Our facilities include Advanced Edit Suite, Shasun News Room, Computer Graphics Lab, Drawing Lab, Shoot Floor and Dubbing Room along with the Sound Recording Room. Moreover, the students benefit from regular seminars and workshops conducted by the department inviting eminent industry professionals. This exposure helps them stay updated with the latest trends and practices in the field of visual communication, preparing them for successful careers.
Our esteemed faculty, advanced facilities and industry connections provide an unparalleled environment for aspiring media professionals. Thus, the Department of Visual Communication (Shift II) at Shasun Jain College for Women aims to provide a comprehensive education that combines rigorous academic training with extensive practical experience.
The Department of Visual Communication at Shri Shankarlal Sundarbai Shasun Jain College for Women, established in the year 2005 caters to sculpt students as media professionals, creators, and effective communicators.
The three-year UG program equips the students with theoretical as well as practical cognition and allows them to make a mark in the field of designing, animation, visualization, photography, reporting, web designing, film making, television production, content writing, editing, art direction and many more.
Their classroom training is a combination of traditional teaching along with ICT-based teaching methods. The students are also exposed to eminent industry professionals through seminars and workshops.
The key elements that comprise the department are the infrastructural facilities that offer hands-on experience to our students. title: Apollo Shine
text:
Apollo Shine

Home

Campus

Apollo Shine

The Apollo SHINE Foundation is a not-for-profit initiative by the Apollo Hospitals group that focuses on Campus Health across 100 plus campuses and covers close to two lakh students in India. The program is designed to create awareness about common health problems and to enable students to be completely equipped to handle different types of medical/health care situations that might arise during their life.

The program has been mandated with the clear objective of taking the tenets of healthy living to the students and sowing the seeds of good health among the youth of India. Through the Shine Foundations the college will be a part of several activities related to healthcare and wellness including health checkups, awareness talks, life support training, health related events, health audits etc.

Given the COVID-19 pandemic, the Apollo SHINE Foundation has revamped the program to ensure campuses are prepared to deal with health issues as effectively as possible. The following facilities are available at the campus,

Campus Safety Audit by the Shine Medical Team

Personalized recommendation and guidelines post-audit

Covid vaccination

Referral services

Health and Safety protocols

Health Awareness talks and webinars

Annual Medi-screen for students and staff

Emergency preparedness and First Aid Room on campus manned by an experienced nursing officer

Shine Card benefits for students and staff inclusive of the immediate family members.

In-hospital assistance in Apollo hospitals across India

Shasun Jain College is glad to collaborate with Apollo Shine and working together on this mission to
#KeepIndiaHealthy.
In addition to meeting the basic and most common needs of the students they serve, campus health-service programs also act as referral agents for students to connect with medical providers, as needed, in the local community. The goal is to help the students understand as much of the healthcare system as possible so that when they step out of college they are equipped to make the right decisions to help SAVE A LIFE. At the very least, they will be an authority on healthy choices. They will know how to choose a doctor and when to rush to a hospital. They will understand their body better and the reasons they should avoid medicines.

Campus Company

Retro Shop

On December 19, 2022, Our Secretary Madam, Smt. Usha Abhaya Srisrimal, and Associate Secretary, Dr. Harish L Metha, opened ten small campus businesses in retro model shops. The major goal is to provide the aspiring business owners with practical business experience. For a period of 11 months, alumni and current students are given the chance to effectively run a business on campus. Additionally, Shabash ED cell supports them in expanding their business outside of the college.

Vending Stall

Shabash promotes and encourages budding entrepreneurs to take up the Vend in stalls inside campus. It is a platform to exhibit and enhance the Marketing skill of the budding Entrepreneurs. It gives an opportunity to every student to learn the skill of entrepreneurship. Equal opportunities will be given to all interested students to run the vend in stall throughout the year with stalls like Textiles, Food stall, Jewellery Nail art, Mehandi, Accessories, etc. These vend in stalls help them to gain business knowledge and gives them the confidence to become future entreprenuers.

Shabash has initiated a transmission of physical vend in stall to virtual platform by onboarding our students creative products and services in the online portal of Shasun Bazaar.stores through Instamogo. It facilitates a real time experience and global exposure. The number of products in the virtual store on board by our students were more than 800+ products in the categories of handcrafts, textiles, jewellery, Cakes and homemade chocolates, Herbal products like Neem soaps, Aloe Vera body lotion, Herbal shampoo, services like wedding planners and event management.

Shabash has initiated during this pandemic a transmission of physical vend in stall to virtual platform by onboarding our students creative products and services in the online portal of Shasun Bazaar.stores through Instamogo. It facilitates a real time experience and global exposure. The number of products in the virtual store on boarded by our students were more than 800+ products in the categories of handcrafts, textiles, jewelry, Cakes and homemade chocolates, Herbal products like Neem soaps, Alovela body lotion, Herbal shampoo, services like wedding planners and event management.

Aavin Parlour –Startup Campus Business

Aavin is a Co-operative Government unit which was setup in the year 2018 in our college campus by Shabash- An Entrepreneur Development Cell. It was established for the purpose of encouraging the students to develop and learn the entrepreneur skills through managing the Aavin parlour inside the campus. Aspiring entrepreneur students were taken as interns to run the Aavin parlour by Shabash. The students were trained for a period of 3 months and a certificate was issued by the college on the successful completion of the training period. The Aavin parlour operated between 9am to 5pm by shift I & II students.

Students have gained various kinds of practical knowledge to run the business themselves which gives them the confidence to take up as a startup by the motivation of Shabash. Around 55 students have successfully completed their internships in Aavin from July 2018 – March 2020.

The Aavin parlour which was established by the college has generated good profit and the student interns were able to learn generation of profits and manage the business.

Shabash has initiated to give incubation business opportunities to alumni students who have completed their internship in Aavin in the year 2020-21. The management was magnanimous to accept the startup proposal of Aavin by Shasuneon entrepreneurs inside the college campus. The college has facilitated with the security deposit Rs.20, 000 for Aavin and also contributed Rs.20,000 towards Seed capital for the students to support them to become an entrepreneur.

Shabash Incubation Centre

Shabash Incubation Centre is an idea generation hub to trigger the innovative ideas for an incubation startup. Incubation hub facilitates activities like mentoring workshops, live demo projects, model projects, B-plan competitions, Idea generation competition, etc.
The incubation centre will facilitate the students with the development of proto type products and support them with the necessary technology. The college will provide financial support in the incubation stage of the product development. The college will also help the student to obtain the patent right for the innovative product developed by the students in the incubation centre.

It is the most popular location on campus, not only for physical refreshment but also for student bonding and discussions.

The College canteen is one of the busiest spots in the campus. The canteen is located on the ground floor of Building III of the College. The canteen has a large kitchen, and the kitchen staff goes out of their way to provide students and staff with nutritious and hygienic food on campus. Our canteen strives to offer a wide range of high-quality food and beverages at reasonable prices. Students receive subsidized food from 7.30 a.m. to 6.30 p.m.

The Canteen served a variety of Jain food to the students and staff of the College. It also provides refreshment like fresh Juices, snack items, sandwiches, beverages etc. Food items are prepared with RO treated water. RO water purifiers are also installed in the Canteen.

Functioning of Canteen

A team of staff members monitor the hygiene condition of the Canteen.

The College conducts a survey on the quality of food every semester

Based on the survey feedback the services are improved in order to cater to the needs of students

The Canteen Committee members supervise the overall functioning of the canteen

The wastage of vegetables, food and plastic are segregated for disposal.

COE-A&C of Shri Shankarlal Sundarbai Shasun Jain College for Women is the first to win the Grant for the production of new dance-dramas by Tamil Nadu Eyal Isai Nataka Mandram. 50 students performed in the dance drama ‘Kudumba Vilakku’,Tamil poet Bharathidasan.
National Symposium
The Centre of Excellence, Art & Culture in Collaboration with Bharata Ilango Foundation for Asian Culture (BIFAC), conducted a unique virtual National Symposium ‘Kala Samanvaya 2020′ on December 11, 12 & 13, 2020. It was specially curated by Dr. Padma Subrahmanyam, (Padma Bhushan Awardee), Managing Trustee, BIFAC.
Three stalwarts Satavadhani Dr R. Ganesh, Dr R. Nagaswamy, (Padma Bhushan Awardee) & Dr S. Krishnaswamy (Padma Shri Awardee) gave illuminating talks on different aspects of art, showcasing the commonalities between the traditions of North & South India, between the Marga (Classical) & Desi (Regional) and the impact of Bharateeya traditions on the entire South East Asia.
The Valedictory Address was by Shri Ashish Khokar, Editor, Dancer & Curator, MKDC, IGNCA Delhi who effectively summed up the proceedings of the 3 days.
International Conference
A two-day International Conference on ‘Mythology: In Literature and Culture’(Western and Indian Approaches) was organised by the Centre of Excellence-Art and Culture with the Department of B.A English on 24th and 25th February, 2021 through online mode.
It included a series of lectures by experts in the field followed by paper presentations by Faculty members, PG students and research scholars from various educational institutions across India. The Day 1 eminent speakers on the Western approach of the topic were Dr. S. Armstrong Head, Dept of English, University of Madras, Dr. E. Raja Rao, Visiting Professor, Dept of English, Central University of Odisha and Ms. Cauvery Madhavan, Author, Ireland. The emphasis on Day 2 was on the Indian approach and the experts were Ms. Usha Narayan, Author, Chennai, Dr. D.K. Hari and Dr. Hema Hari, Founders, Bharat Gyan. The Valedictory address was given by Dr. Jeffery D.Long, Elizabethtown College, Pennsylvania, USA. The deliberations of the conference enabled the participants and scholars to understand the influence of myth on language, literature and culture in everyday life.
The Young Researchers Forum
‘The Young Researchers Forum’, (TYRF) a platform for research presentations in collaboration with Nrithyodaya–The Academy of Performing Arts (NAPA), Mumbai was inaugurated by Padma Bhushan Dr. Padma Subrahmanyam & Padma Shri Sekhar Sen ji, Former Chairman, Sangeet Natak Akademi & successfully completed an impressive 18 sessions. It introduces two scholars per month, each session featuring one junior researcher presenting the article and one expert adding input to it.

title: Equal Opportunities Cell
text:
Equal Opportunities Cell

Home

Shasun Suraksha

Equal Opportunities Cell

Our College has initiated the Equal Opportunity Cell to ensure that all students are treated as equal and attempts to address deep-seated inequalities in our system. The cell was inaugurated on 8
th
February 2021 by IQAC Director Ms. N.M. Kavitha. A webinar on “Up-Skilling for Competitiveness and Employability” was conducted for our students and Dr. Kishor Budda, Career Guidance Cell – Director, GITAM University was the Resource Person. Nearly 1265 students enthusiastically participated and were benefitted through it.

Equal Opportunity Cell works for affirmative actions for the deprived sections such as persons from SC, ST, OBC (Non-creamy layer) categories, persons from religious minorities, differently-abled persons and so on. It also guides weaker section students to avail the permissible scholarships and financial assistance and other facilities and privileges.

Our college has always ensured that differently abled and other weaker section students stay ahead in their learning process. Faculty pay more attention to their special needs and provide them with more encouragement and support. Also, the College makes it their prerogative to provide scribes for the differently abled students during University Exams.

Purpose :

To ensure that all the students are treated equally and to address any issues raised.

To ensure that the disadvantaged/minority groups such as SC/ST/OBC are given equal importance in all aspects of the learning process.

To prevent any type of harassment against the minority/disadvantaged groups.

To infuse unity in diversity among the students, teaching and non-teaching staff and to eliminate the perception of discrimination.

To ensure that there is no discrimination in terms of religion, race, caste, disability etc.

To provide auxiliary support towards skill development that enhances the employability and to meet the distinct needs of students.

Equal Opportunity Cell Policy

title: Faculty Training Programme on Indian Knowledge Systems
text:
Name of the Event
: Faculty Training Programme on Indian Knowledge Systems

Date of Event
: 10.11.25

Guests
:

Padmashri Awardee Dr. M. D. Srinivas

Founding Chairman, Centre for Policy Studies, Chennai

Dr. K.S. Balasubramanian

Director, The Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, Chennai

Dr. Saraswathi Murali

Chartered Accountant & Information Systems Auditor

Description

Summary

A Faculty Training Programme on Bharatiya Jnana Parampara (Indian Knowledge Tradition) was organized on 10th November 2025 for the faculty members by the Centre for Excellence for Art and Culture in collaboration with the Internal Quality Assurance Cell (IQAC) of the college. The Resource Person of the first session Padma Shri Awardee Dr. M.D. Srinivas, Former Head, Department of Theoretical Physics, University of Madras, and Founding Chairman of the Centre for Policy Studies, Chennai spoke about the rich corpus of Indian Knowledge Systems, emphasizing India’s manuscript heritage, epigraphical wealth, and its far-reaching contributions to global scientific thought. He highlighted rare sources such as the Tamil numerical text Chudamani Ullamudiyan and the Sanskrit Katapayadi Sankhya system, elaborating on their role in decoding astronomical data related to stars and constellations. He further explained, how ancient Indian discoveries influenced Greek and Western astronomers, and illustrating the depth of India’s intellectual legacy.

The second session was conducted by Dr. K.S. Balasubramanian, Director, The Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, who delivered a thought-provoking lecture on the Life Sciences of Ancient Bharat. Citing references from the Mahabharata, the Garbha Upanishad, and the life of Mahavira, he discussed the profound understanding of cytology, genetics, and embryology evident in India’s classical texts. His talk drew connections between ancient scriptural knowledge and modern biological sciences, highlighting India’s early engagement with scientific inquiry.

The third session featured Dr. Saraswathi Murali, Chartered Accountant, who spoke on “Influence of Kautilya’s Arthashastra on Modern Accounting and Revenue Administration.” She examined how Kautilya’s Arthashastra discusses principles of fraud prevention, accounting errors, revenue collection, audit procedures, and administrative accountability, emphasizing its relevance to contemporary financial management and ethics.

Faculty members from several leading institutions—including Ethiraj College for Women, A.M. Jain College, D.G. Vaishnav College, and M.O.P. Vaishnav College—participated enthusiastically, along with the faculty of Shasun Jain College.

Outcome

The day-long training programme provided an enriching academic platform that seamlessly integrated India’s ancient wisdom with modern educational perspectives, inspiring faculty to explore and incorporate the essence of Bharatiya Jnana Parampara in teaching and research.

On the occasion of International Women’s Day, Shri Shankarlal Sundarbai Shasun Jain College for Women, T. Nagar, Chennai, celebrated the achievements and resilience of women by honouring renowned Bharatanatyam exponent Dr. Roja Kannan with the “Shasun Sreshta Stree” Award.

Dr. Roja Kannan stands as one of the most distinguished exponents of Bharatanatyam from Chennai, with an illustrious career spanning over five decades. Known for her pristine style and expressive depth, she has captivated audiences through numerous performances and lecture demonstrations across India and abroad.

Addressing the gathering, Dr. Roja Kannan shared inspiring reflections from her personal journey. Through her heartfelt words, she spoke about the challenges she faced in life, including her courageous battle with cancer, and how determination, faith, and dedication to her art helped her overcome adversity. Her story of resilience deeply moved the audience and served as a powerful message of hope and strength for the students.

Smt. Usha Abhaya Kumar, Secretary of Shasun Jain College for Women, felicitated Dr. Roja Kannan and presented the Shasun Sreshta Stree Award in recognition of her outstanding contribution to the field of Bharatanatyam and Indian cultural heritage and blessed students on International women’s day.

Outcome:

The programme fostered a sense of empowerment, inspiration, and respect for women achievers among the students.

title: Margazhi Festival
text:
Name of the Event
: Margazhi Festival

Date of Event
: 03.01.26 – 10.01.26

Description

Summary

The Centre for Excellence in Art and Culture celebrated Margazhi Utsav 2026, marking the auspicious Tamil month of Margazhi (Mārgaśīrṣa), a period deeply revered for its spiritual and cultural significance.

A major highlight of the festival was the collective rendition of the Tiruppāvai by the students of the Centre for Excellence in Art and Culture. Rendered in the true spirit of bhakti and seva, the sacred hymns of Āṇḍāḷ—traditionally sung during Margazhi—set a deeply devotional tone and sanctified the proceedings.

The festival witnessed the enthusiastic participation of 58 budding artistes, including students trained under Guru Lalita Ganapathy, Guru Suvasini, Mrs. Kamali, Dr. Ramakrishnan Neelamani, and Dr. Lakshmi Jayapriya. The students showcased a vibrant array of performances encompassing Carnatic vocal music, classical dance, instrumental recitals, and the traditional folk art of Kolattam, reflecting their rigorous training and artistic dedication.

The young artistes were honoured and encouraged by the esteemed presence of Guru Lalita Ganapathy, senior disciple of Padmavibhushan Dr. Padma Subramaniam; Mridangam Vidwan Dr. Ramakrishnan Neelamani; and Dr. Ramadevi Sekhar, Director, Centre for Excellence in Art and Culture. Their participation added scholarly depth and spiritual inspiration to the event.

Margazhi Utsav 2026 provided a valuable and prestigious platform for budding artistes to present their talents. Overall, the festival was imbued with devotion, enthusiasm, and artistic fervor, significantly enriching the cultural ambience of the campus.

Outcome

This is a great opportunity for the young artists to showcase their talents.

title: Mother Language Day
text:
Name of the Event
: Mother Language Day

Date of Event
: 21/02/2026

Description

Summary

The Department of Tamil (Shift I) celebrated World Mother Language Day with great enthusiasm. The programme aimed to create awareness about the importance of preserving and promoting mother languages. Our distinguished alumna, Ms. Shobana Swaminathan, was the Chief Guest for the event. She completed her B.Com in Corporate Secretaryship in 2022 and M.Com in Accounting and Finance in 2024. She is currently working as an Accounts Payable Associate at Accenture. She also served as the judge for the competitions and motivated the students with her inspiring speech.

Three competitions were conducted, and nearly 100 students actively participated.The programme was organized smoothly and helped students gain more knowledge about the significance of World Mother Language Day.

The event concluded successfully and achieved its objective of spreading awareness about the importance of mother languages. Overall, the programme was a grand success.

title: Green Campus
text:
Green Campus

Home

Campus

Green Campus

Greenery
in the campus is focussed upon. All available space has been utilized to make the campus green. The College premises has a range of fruit trees, flowering plants, and herbal plants. Couroupita guianensis (Nagalinga Tree), Millingtonia hortensis (Maramalli), Crape Jasmine, Pyrethrum Root Plant, False Daisy, Lemon Grass, Almond Tree, Polyalthia, Custard Apple, Sammanthi, Arali, Thotta sinungi, Sembaruthi, Murungai, Siriya nangai, Vilvam, Pinna maram, Athi (Fig Tree), Aralia, Arasa maram, Poovarasa maram, Thennai maram, Mango tree, Magizhampoo, Money plant, Ashoka tree, Marigold (Samanthi), Naval maram, Koyyaa maram, Nochi chedi, Nithyakalyani, Nandhiyavattai, Idli Poo, Vazhaimaram – Banana tree, Karpoora valli contribute to the green cover of the campus.

Herbal Garden & Vermicompost

The institution has a
Herbal garden
. Holy Basil, Karisalankanni, Mint Basil, Vallarai, Mudakathan, Vetrilai (Betel Leaf), Pirandai, Thoothuvalai, Aloe vera, Nellikai (Amla), Siruneeraga kal aalai, Karpoora valli, Neem Tree, Pottia (Poovarasam Maram) and Rain Tree are tended to with care by a dedicated gardener and overseen by the Facilities Team. Students of the college water the plants on a daily basis. Vertical Garden has been created. Piping work for drip irrigation is in place for efficient water conservation. Drips will be created using old plastic bottles by students. Vermicompost pit is being installed to reuse garbage collected around the campus (dry leaves and twigs). It will function from the academic year 2021-22.

We consider it our best practice to give the saplings grown in the campus to Chief Guests and Resource Persons of all college and department activities as a memento. These saplings are given to the guests in paper bags made from handmade paper by the students of the college.

The greenery adds to the aesthetics of the campus and the Management takes personal interest to constantly enhance and adorn the premises.

GO GREEN Bio–Gas plant

Aim

Biogas project
is Eco-Friendly project. It is to utilize the food waste into renewable energy. It helps to produce organic fertilizers , which in turn we use to generate manure to green plants. The fertilizer discharge from the digester can accelerate plant growth and resilience to diseases.

Brief

collect vegetable waste from outside from Vegetable market (T.Nagar railway station) and inside college

Bio-gas

The Bio-gas Plant was started on 1
st
of June 2018, by Enactus Shasun. Vegetable waste has been collected from Vegetable Vendors of Ranganathan street near T.Nagar railway station to feed the Bio-gas plant . The plant is usually fed with 40 to 50 Kg. of vegetable waste per day, which gives on an average of 2 to 3 Kg of gas per day. The gas generated has been used by the college canteen to boil 20 to 30 liters of milk in the morning and in the evening and also for cooking rice. The canteen is using on an average of 1.5 to 2 Kg. of gas per day

The canteen uses 20 Kg per month then it has saved almost Rs. 700 per month. From the month of June ’18 to Nov’18 it has used 92 Kg of gas , where it costs Rs. 3,220

Benefit of this Project

(For collecting the vegetable waste we have appointed 1 person by paying 1000/- pm )

Campus

Infrastructure

Shasun campus spreads over 2.1 acres in a beautiful atmosphere ideally suited for education in the heart of the Chennai city. The infrastructure and facilities available on campus are amongst the very best. It is a wholly self-contained campus comprising everything that students on campus would ever require.

It has 3 buildings with lift along with Central Instrumentation Facility, Computer labs, Arts, Science and Commerce departments, Classrooms, Staffrooms. Canteen facility and Gym.

All the class rooms are furnished with LCD projector and Green board.
There are 7 labs overall, which are equipped with approximately 362 computers and 8 projectors with high bandwidth internet.
All the computers in the laboratories are equipped with the latest hardware and software systems which are updated regularly to cater to the current demands.

The college has a fully furnished lab for students of ID & D to explore their designing and creative skills. The campus has an air-conditioned seminar hall that can seat 150 people. It is used for guest lectures, seminars or intercollegiate competitions.

The college houses an open auditorium of around 9600 sq. ft, spacious enough to accommodate around 800 – 900 people. The space creates a close to heart ambience, while staging various events and program.

The Media Labs under the Department of Visual Communication is fully equipped with state-of-the-art studio facilities consisting of a shooting floor for television production, edit suite, audio recording and voice booth, photography studio with darkroom lab, drawing studio, graphic designing and multimedia lab.

About IQAC
“Quality is not an act, it’s a habit”. – Aristotle
The IQAC of the college was established on 17th November 2006 after a year’s time of inspection of the college. The prime task of the IQAC is to develop a system for conscious, consistent and catalytic improvement in the overall performance of the Institution. The cell precisely plans the quality initiatives of the institution by ensuring the quality culture, institutionalizing and internalizing quality parameters in adherence to the norms of National Assessment and Accreditation Council of India. The IQAC reviews the academic and administrative quality processes of the institution periodically and takes necessary action for the continual improvement of the services offered by the institution.
Since quality enhancement is a continuous process, IQAC meets regularly, conducts academic and administrative audits and ensures timely submission of records to accreditation and ranking bodies.
We, at Shasun, never compromise in quality, and thus we have established an Internal Quality Assurance Cell (IQAC) as per the requirements and guidelines of the National Assessment and Accreditation Council (NAAC).
Composition of IQAC
As per the revised NAAC framework 2017, the composition of the IQAC members was made. IQAC is constituted under the Chairmanship of the Head of the institution with heads of major academic and administrative units, a few teachers, distinguished educationists, representatives of local management and stakeholders.
The following are the members of the IQAC:
Internal Team Structure
Our Vision
To develop a system for conscious, consistent and catalytic improvement in the overall quality of the institution.
Our Mission
To ensure timely, efficient and progressive performance of academic and administrative tasks. To ensure the adequacy, maintenance and functions of the support structure and services. To explore and integrate modern methods of teaching, learning and assessment. To collaborate with other institutions and industries for research and skill development. To develop credible evaluation procedures for the quality enhancement of academic, research and administrative activities.
Our Objectives
Development and application of quality benchmarks/parameters for various academic and administrative activities of the institution. Facilitating the creation of a learner-centric environment conducive to quality education and training the faculty to adopt the required knowledge and technology for participatory teaching and learning process. Arrangement for feedback response from students, parents and other stakeholders on quality-related institutional processes. Dissemination of information on various quality parameters of higher education. Organization of inter and intra institutional workshops, seminars on quality related themes and promotion of quality circles. Documentation of the various programmes/activities leading to quality improvement. Acting as a nodal agency of the Institution for coordinating quality-related activities, including adoption and dissemination of best practices. Development and maintenance of institutional database through MIS for the purpose of maintaining/enhancing the institutional quality. Development of Quality Culture in the institution. Preparation of the Annual Quality Assurance Report (AQAR) as per guidelines and parameters of NAAC, to be submitted to NAAC.

title: ISO
text:
ISO

Home

ISO

ISO Cell

The college has established an ISO 9001 Cell for its Quality Management Systems. All the systems and procedures of all academic departments, administration, examination, physical education, library, placement and training, purchase and stores are established, completely documented and maintained as per requirements of International Standard ISO 9001 : 2015 Quality Management Systems.

ISO Composition

Dr. S. Padmavathi -
Principal

Dr.S.Rukmani -
Vice Principal

Dr. R. Revathy -
MR

As per the standard requirements, Dr.R.Revathy has been appointed as the Management Representative for the establishment, implementation and maintenance of the ISO 9001 QMS. In addition to this, every department/section has got its own ISO 9001 Coordinators as well as trained internal quality auditors selected from among the faculty and staff members.

Principal and Vice Principal with the assistance of the Management Representative, plan and organize periodic internal quality audits and management review meetings. Internal quality audits are cross functional audits and Vice Principal deputes trained auditors to various departments for conducting the audits as per schedule. Periodic inputs are obtained from the departments for discussion in management review meetings. The management review meetings and internal quality audits are scheduled once in six months. The meetings are chaired by Principal, Vice Principal and attended by Management Representative, HODs, ISO Coordinators and Internal Quality Auditors. HODs and ISO Coordinators ensure that all systems and procedures in the departments along with the corresponding documents and records are maintained as per the requirements of ISO 9001, and are produced for verification for external and internal quality audits.

Continuous improvement is an ongoing process. The audit findings are rectified, suitable decisions are taken for the issues related to achievement of objectives and periodic revisions of documented procedures are also carried out.

Quality Policy

Solid Waste Management – Institutional Social Responsibility
Solid waste management is the biggest challenge for Governments world over. Recycling of this solid waste material is a challenge due to the volume of debris that is collected on a daily basis. In Chennai, Urbaser Sumeet is the waste management and recycling collection unit which is an operation under Greater Chennai Corporation. The garbage collected from households is dumped into Micro Compost Centre in burial grounds across the city.
In an effort to work hand-in-hand with GCC and provide a viable solution to the humongous task of recycling of solid waste. Shri Shankarlal Sundarbai Shasun Jain College for Women signed a contract with Greater Chennai Corporation to setup the Micro Compost Centre (MCC) at Kannammapet Burial Ground, T. Nagar.
The College undertook the end-to-end process of collecting the wet waste from Urbaser Sumeet, processing the waste in the MCC to produce organic fertilizer in collaboration with an NGO “Namma Ooru Foundation”. Following an analysis of the facility, “Windrow composting” was implemented to produce quality compost.
Our Vision
To rejuvenate the Mother Earth.
Our Mission
By creating and disseminating knowledge in solid waste management to students by providing unique learning and experiencing in SWM process.

Messages

Secretary’s Message

“Education is the most powerful weapon which you can use to change the world” – Nelson Mandela

Shri Shankarlal Sundarbai Shasun Jain College for Women is located in the heart of Chennai and has been constantly working for the empowerment of women through education. Our college has been a crucial platform in career building for thousands of students. Reputed for its high standards in higher studies, the college is continuously attracting most of the major recruiters in its placement drive. This builds a good bond between the college, students, and the industries.

The student-centric academic structure aims at the overall development of the students. It also aims at developing outstanding professional skills. The co-curricular and extra-curricular activities develop versatility in students. The college provides the space for enhancing various skills like sports, arts, martial art forms, etc. It also provides a student-friendly environment to make the learning process much easier. The college provides the space for enhancing various skills like sports, arts, martial art forms, etc. It also provides a student-friendly environment to make the learning process much easier. The college gives a lot of opportunities to students to enhance their skills and also implement them.

– Smt. Usha Abhaya Srisrimal, (Secretary)

Associate Secretary’s Message

“An investment in knowledge pays the best interest” – Benjamin Franklin

Rising steadily from a very modest beginning point, SHRI SHANKARLAL SUNDARBAI SHASUN JAIN COLLEGE FOR WOMEN has now grown into a prominent educational institution making learning a cheerful reality for many erudite minds.

Over the years, Shasun College has made innumerable, positive contributions to the academic circles. Our students, proudly identified as SHASUNEONS amongst us, have taken it upon themselves to deliver their best versions at various intra- and inter-collegiate competitions, and have won laurels for the same. A youthful student community, sprightly and savvy, backed up a qualified faculty community, solid and sorted, has jointly led us through the institution’s path towards its grandness today. It is sheer passion and commitment put into the art of educating that has made it possible for us to ascend heights, touched never before.

The dream of becoming a world-class academic institution continues on and I solicit your support in the affirmation of the same as we tread on a long, long journey. Everyone under the Shasun umbrella is in fact, instrumental in the spirited pursuit of this dream. Come, let us all bind ourselves to the right course of action and stay determined in providing a learning experience that encourages versatility and scholarship.

– Harish L Metha, (Associate Secretary)

Hon Secretary General’s Message

Greetings!
I am proud to state that our college is endowed with a progressive futuristic outlook that aims at continual growth in the quality of all academic activities with a sense of commitment to fully meet the expectations of the students, parents, and society at large.
Foresight, ability to seize the opportunity, relentless drive to succeed and tremendous acumen in recognizing the needs of the industry and integrating knowledge with professional inputs are the secrets behind Shasun. This motive has always kept us at the forefront of Education, Value Creation, and a Sustainable model of growth and achievement for the past decade.
The caring faculty, state of art infrastructure, and friendly academic environment make the college different and a respectable institution in the field of education.

The student-centric academic structure aims at the overall development of the students and also in developing outstanding professional skills. The co-curricular and extra-curricular activities develop versatile students who actively contribute a lot in their professional and social life.
We welcome you at Shasun to dream, imagine and explore and assure you an unforgettable learning experience and join us in making it a truly world-class institution.
All the best for your exciting career!

– Abhaya Srisrimal Jain, (Hon Secretary General)

Principal’s Message

A Chinese proverb says “If you are planning for a year, sow rice: if you are planning for a decade, plant trees; if you are planning for a lifetime, educate people”. There is no greater impact than empowering people through education. College is a place where a person finds the transformation of oneself into mature, responsible and become an independent adult. Shasun family assures a student to learn more and march towards improving knowledge, develop skills and prepare for the future. The college not only focuses on the theoretical curriculum, but also help in personal development through extra- curricular activities, creating successful entrepreneurs and by empowering an individual into a good leader.
Our college provides modern day teaching methods, plentiful library resources, placement cell and more other benefits for staff and students. We also offer series of programmes, club activities and forum for teachers to upgrade their intellectual leadership in higher education and through sincere utilisation of the e-resources.

We serve the learner community and provide great support during the tough times. Our mission is to protect students through POSH cell an initiative to prevent sexual harassment against women. We also motivate our students through ‘Yuva Shakti club’ to improve and showcase their inherent talents and skills.
I finally believe that our college is more than just a place to learn. It provides the scope by equipping with everything that a student needs to achieve excellence. There is an assurance that our goal and mission on offering value education would transcend much beyond just awarding degree certificate to students.
I wish our students to discover the true meaning, purpose and fulfilment of life and endeavour in all walks of life.

– Dr. S. Padmavathi, (Principal)

Vice Principal’s Message

The highest education is that which does not merely give us information but makes our life in harmony with all existence-Gurudev Rabindranath Tagore.
This is the kind of education we strive to impart in Shri Shankarlal Sundarbai Shasun Jain College for Women .Today, Shasun College has evolved into a gateway to excellence. We not only prove ourselves in academics but also in co-curricular and extra-curricular activities. The Centres of Excellence crowns it all.A look at the many university rank holders across departments,

the numerous distinguished visitors, the multitude of clubs and forums and the innumerable multifarious activities that the college is buzzing with bears testimony to the rich tapestry that characterises Shri Shankarlal Sundarbai Shasun Jain College for Women. Teaching-Learning is at the core of the institutional ethos. We follow a student-centric approach. Teachers are trained as empowered agents to bring social change.

The classroom is looked upon as a site of engaged learning, reflective action and participatory pedagogy. We have ICT enabled classrooms. We also take pride in being an environmentally conscious institution. We have been taking several initiatives to provide a clean and green campus .The college, while proud of its past achievements, is marching ahead on its journey to achieve excellence.

– Dr. S. Rukmani, (Vice Principal)

The Shasun jain college cadets successfully completed their B and C certificate Exam every year .
Trainees also get some extra marks in the department of telecommunication and few other public sectors after achieving ‘B’ certificate in NCC. 75% of total training.
Certificate – B : It can be taken by SD/SW cadets of the NCC, after class year 10 and those studying for a degree. The candidate must have attended a minimum 75% of total training periods laid down in the syllabus for the first and second years of SD/SW NCC (All Wings). The cadet must have attended one Annual Training Camp/NIC. Cadets who possess Certificate – A will be awarded 10 bonus marks. An air wing cadet must do a minimum 10 Glider launches. Certificate – C : Is the highest level certificate for NCC cadets. It can be taken in the 3rd• year of training, in the 3rd year of degree course. Those who possess a Certificate – B can take it in the first year after their +2, and in the 1st year of their degree. The cadet must have attended two Annual Training Camps or one Annual Training Camp and one of the following: RD Camp Delhi, Centrally Organised Camp, Para Training Camp, Attachment Training with service units, National Integration Camp, Youth Exchange Programme, or Foreign Cruise (Navy Wing only).
Grading in Certificate Three certificates are awarded (1) A grade, (2) B grade, (3) C grade. The best certificate is A, which has the highest value. (i) A cadet has to obtain 45% marks in each paper & 50% marks in the aggregate to pass the examination. Grading is based on total marks obtain will be awarded as follows. (aa) Grading ‘A’ – Cadets obtaining 80% marks and above. (ab) Grading ‘B’ – Cadets obtaining 65% marks and above but below 80%. (ac) Grading ‘C’ – Cadets obtaining 50% marks and above but below 65%. (ad) Fail – Cadets obtaining less than 45% in any paper or less than 50% in aggregate.

title: NSS - Shasun College
text:
NSS
Home
Life @ Shasun
Centre for Extension Activities
Objectives
The concept of National Service Scheme was started in the year 1969 to build a sense of social responsibility through teacher and students involvement in constructive service with the motto of “Not Me but You”. NSS volunteers work in rural areas, adopted villages and schools to serve the cause of society through survey, education and health awareness programmes.
Aim of NSS
The overall aim of the National Service Scheme as envisaged earlier, is to give an extension dimension to the higher education system and orient the student youth to community service while they are studying in educational institutions.
Milestones
The concept of making National Service a part of University Education took about 20 years to evolve from the state of an idea into that of a scheme. The early seeds of it were sown by Dr. S. Radhakrishnan in 1948.
Our Objectives
To understand themselves and their community in which they work.
Identify the needs and problems of the community and involve them in problem solving.
Develop among themselves a sense of social and civic responsibility.
Utilize their knowledge in finding practical solutions to individual and community problems.
Develop competence required for group – living and sharing of Responsibilities.
Gain skills in mobilizing community participation.
Acquire leadership qualities and democratic attitudes.
Develop capacity to meet emergencies and natural disasters and practice national integration and social harmony.

text:
Overview
Home
Life @ Shasun

Newsletter

The existence of the College is the outcome of single minded dedication of many kind hearts. The Institution considers it their moral responsibility to carry forward this baton of good work and hand it over to the next generation. Who can be better recipients than the souls that drank from the pond! Shasun founded the Centre of Extension Activities to kindle the service mind in the students and feed their constant craving for knowledge and exposure.
Extension programmes of Shasun are ‘learnings taking place beyond the classrooms’ and augment the sense of compassion for others. It helps to build relationships while working with NGOs, government agencies, companies, etc. It affirms to make a difference when they do something with what they have learnt.
The college has adopted Kaliyanur Village, Kanchipuram District and dedicated efforts on the part of the institution have gone into enhancing the infrastructure of the corporation school, the public library and toilets. Students of our college celebrate significant traditional days and festivals with the students and general public of Kaliyanur Village.
The numerous clubs of Shasun and the various departments involve themselves in extension activities to create a social connect and community engagement.
Highlights
Students volunteered for Covid-19 Contact Virtual Tracing work for Greater Chennai Corporation. The students worked from home during July and August 2020. They provided moral support and guidance for the patients. The contribution of the students was recognised through remuneration from GCC and certificates from Chennai Volunteers. During the two months of volunteering, the students reached out to 10,000 COVID-19 positive patients.
Under the PLANT A TREE! GREEN THE EARTH! Initiative of Environment Club, students distribute saplings to the general public in their neighbourhood. The initiative was kick-started on 16th September 2020 on the occasion of World Ozone Day focussing on “Let the Green be Seen”. The club members distribute saplings on a monthly basis as an initiative to increase the awareness on the importance of greenery.
A National Level E-Quiz was organised for students of various colleges to celebrate the International Yoga Day, 21st June 2020 on the topic “Let’s Get Acquainted with Yoga”.
RRC students distributed food packets to the needy people to commemorate World Food Day on 16th October 2020. Food was distributed in areas such as Ambattur, Kolathur, Sembakkam, Sowcarpet, Poonamallee, Valasaravakkam, Pallawaram, KK Nagar, West Mambalam, and Kodambakam.
The club also organized competitions such as drawing, elocution, essay writing and poetry writing for Government school students in Sholinganallur, Chemmencherry & Perumbakkam on account of National Youth Day. The topic for the competitions was “My Perception in Shaping New India”.
NSS volunteers and Program Officers created awareness to among neighbours, friends and relatives residing in various areas by explaining about the problems caused by the dreadful COVID-19 virus. Significance of social distancing and sanitizing was explained to the public by the NSS team.
Programs such as cyclothon, walkathon and assistive internship training with Chennai Traffic Police of T-Nagar Sub-Division were carried out during the month of January and February 2021.
In October 2020, Rotaract Club started Ariyalam Vanga – Vaaram Oru Mooligai project to create awareness about our traditional medicinal plants. Benefits of each plant are posted in the social media pages of the club on a weekly basis.
On 18th December 2020, club organized a free makeover training session “OPPANAI” for unprivileged students.
The Institution has constructive relationships with other institutions of the locality for working on various outreach and extension activities. The College organizes various interface programmes with the agencies and addresses the academic and career concerns. NSS team of the College is actively engaged in outreach and extension activities such as blood donation camps, temple cleaning and many awareness programmes.

text:
Faculty Training Programme
Event
: Faculty Training Programme
Date of Event
: 04.06.26
Topic:
Indian Knowledge Systems- Interdisciplinary perspective
Guest
: Dr. N. Vaishnavi
Senior Manager-Academics,
Siddhanta Knowledge Foundation
Dr. Sharda Narayanan
Faculty,
Description
Summary
A Faculty Training Programme on Bharatiya Jnana Parampara (Indian Knowledge Tradition) was organized on 4th June 2026 for the faculty members by the Centre for Excellence for Art and Culture in collaboration with the Internal Quality Assurance Cell (IQAC) of the college.
The Resource Person of the first session Dr. N. Vaishnavi ,Senior Manager-Academics of Siddhanta Knowledge Foundation spoke about the Indian Knowledge Systems Interdisciplinary Perspectives,
The second session was conducted by Dr. Sharda Narayanan, Faculty of Siddhanta Knowledge Foundation who delivered a thought-provoking lecture on Integrating the IKS into Curriculum.
A major focus of the lecture was the concept of the Fourfold Puruṣārthas—Dharma, Artha, Kāma, and Mokṣa—which constitute the foundational goals of human life in the Indian philosophical tradition. The speaker explained that these principles offer a comprehensive framework for personal, social, and spiritual development and can serve as guiding values in educational practices.
The lecture further stressed that incorporating Indian Knowledge Systems into higher education aligns with the vision of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, which advocates multidisciplinary learning, experiential education, and the revitalization of India’s intellectual traditions. The speaker encouraged faculty members to design courses, projects, and pedagogical practices that reflect indigenous knowledge, ethical values, sustainability, and holistic well-being.
The session concluded with an engaging discussion on practical strategies for integrating IKS into teaching and learning. Participants gained valuable insights into how the timeless wisdom of the Indian tradition
Outcome:
The day-long training programme provided an enriching academic platform that seamlessly integrated India’s ancient wisdom with modern educational perspectives, inspiring faculty to explore and incorporate the essence of Bharatiya Jnana Parampara in teaching and research.

title: Cheriyal Painting Workshop
text:
Cheriyal Painting Workshop

Event :
Cheriyal Painting Workshop

Date
: 13.08.25 & 14.08.25

Guest :
Shri. Nageswar Rao & Shri.Sai Kiran

Description
: The Internal Quality Assurance Cell and Centre of Excellence – Art & Culture of Shri Shankarlal Sundarbai Shasun Jain College for Women organized a two-day workshop on Cheriyal Painting in collaboration with SPIC MACAY (Society for the Promotion of Indian Classical Music and Culture Amongst Youth) on 13.08.2025 and 14.08.2025.

The resource person Shri. Nageswara Rao, is a renowned artist specializing in Cheriyal painting, a traditional art form from Telangana, India. Belonging to a family deeply rooted in this heritage where both his father and grandfather were State Award winners—Shri Nageswara Rao carries forward a rich artistic legacy. He, along with his son Shri Sai Kiran, actively engaged and trained students during the workshop.

Participants learned the unique techniques of Cheriyal painting, known for its vivid colours, intricate detailing, and storytelling tradition that narrates epics, folklore, and rural life. The art form not only enhances creativity and fine motor skills but also instills a sense of cultural identity and appreciation for traditional craftsmanship.

27 students participated in this workshop experienced the meditative nature of the painting process, which promotes focus, patience, and relaxation, making it both artistically rewarding and personally enriching.

Outcome:

The initiative served as a vibrant platform for young artists to gain hands-on experience, explore a centuries-old tradition, and contribute to the preservation of India's cultural heritage.

: The International Yoga Day is on 20th June 2025 with a special workshop aimed at promoting wellbeing and holistic health among students. The session began on an auspicious note with the lighting of the traditional Kuthuvilakku by Dr. Ramadevi Sekhar, Director of the Centre, & Ms. Srividhya Co-ordinator of the centre, marking the commencement of the academic year’s cultural and spiritual activities.
The Chief Guest, Ms. Bhooma Madhavan, a renowned faculty member from the Krishnamacharya Yoga Mandiram, delivered an enlightening address on the significance of yoga in managing the mind and emotions. She spoke about the three fundamental emotional states—Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas—as described in yogic philosophy. Emphasizing the importance of nurturing a Sattvic (balanced and serene) state of mind, Ms. Madhavan highlighted how such a disposition fosters clarity in decision-making and supports a peaceful and harmonious lifestyle.
The session was further enriched with a live demonstration of yoga practices led by Ms. Madhavan. Participants actively engaged in various breathing techniques, asanas, and mindfulness practices, making the event both interactive and impactful.
The session witnessed the enthusiastic participation of more than 50 students, who found the experience rejuvenating and insightful. The event not only celebrated yoga as a physical practice but also reinforced its deeper connection to mental and emotional wellbeing.

title: Lecture Series on Culture Studies-15
text:
Lecture Series on Culture Studies-15

Event :
Lecture Series on Culture Studies-15

Topic :
Sculpted Divinity: Gods, Puranas & Stories in Sculpture

Date
: 01.09.2025

Guest :
Shri. Dharani Gunasekaran
Founder, Trawell India

Description
: The Internal Quality Assurance Cell in collaboration with the Centre of Excellence – Art & Culture organized a lecture on “Sculpted Divinity: Gods, Puranas & Stories in Sculpture” on 1st September 2025. A total of 41 students actively participated in this Culture Studies lecture series.

The Chief Guest, Shri. Dharani, delivered an insightful session highlighting the richness of Indian sculptures. He explained how sculptures narrate stories from the Puranas and epics, portraying gods, goddesses, and mythological characters with symbolic gestures. He elaborated on how to identify the age of sculptures through their style, detailing of ornaments, drapery, and carving techniques. He also discussed the representation of cloth, tradition, asanas, mudras, hairstyles, and facial expressions, showing how each detail reflects the cultural and spiritual ethos of the period. Shri Dharani further emphasized the aesthetic values, spiritual dimensions, and historical importance embedded in these works of art. His narration brought alive the idea that sculptures are not merely stone carvings but a visual medium of storytelling that connect us with our heritage.

Outcome:

The lecture provided an excellent opportunity for students to gain deeper knowledge and appreciation of sculptures. It enhanced their understanding of the symbolism, cultural significance, and artistic excellence of Indian sculpture traditions.
